clue.text: Splendid mask for an overseer

parts.note: super is an informal word for splendid or excellent
a visor is a face-covering, a kind of mask

explanation.surface: A magnificent disguise chosen for a foreman.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor watches over workers, as an overseer does: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Such a nonpareil

parts.note: a nonpareil has no equal, so it is one of a kind, without any match anywhere

explanation.definitionFit: Something without parallel or peer is one of a kind, the only example of its sort.

clue.text: Guess tea-time's changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone estimates that the hour for afternoon tea has shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the eight letters of TEATIMES; the apostrophe adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to make a rough judgement of a figure, which is to guess it.

clue.text: It's indigenous, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: It's indigenous, in a manner of speaking

parts.words: It's indigenous, in a manner of speaking
parts.note: the everyday phrase 'in a manner of speaking' means 'so to say', but here it literally points to native speech

explanation.surface: A hedged claim that something is native, sort of.
explanation.definitionFit: The vernacular is the native local tongue of a place, its homegrown manner of speech.

clue.text: Gets in a new variety of chairs

indicators.note: a new variety is a fresh arrangement, signalling the letters of the words before are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A shop stocks a novel range of chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new variety of' rearranges GETSINA, the letters of 'Gets in a'; 'a' does double duty in the surface only, here it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Seating is a collective term for chairs and other places to sit.

clue.text: Do boring job —. so much paper!

explanation.surface: A tedious task at the office brings a pile of paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a stray full stop after the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: To ream is to enlarge a hole with a boring tool; a ream is also a quantity of paper, 500 sheets.

clue.text: It may weaken the spirit of even the bravest

definitions.text: It may weaken the spirit of even the bravest

parts.words: It may weaken the spirit of even the bravest
parts.note: spirit here is strong drink, which is weakened by adding water, not courage

explanation.surface: Something that can sap the courage of the boldest person.
explanation.definitionFit: Watering down whisky or gin lowers its strength, so thinning it weakens alcoholic spirit.

clue.text: Ambiguity of the unintelligible Dutch

parts.note: 'double Dutch' is British slang for gibberish, so speech of that sort is double-something

explanation.surface: Complaining that Dutch speakers are vague and incomprehensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double Dutch' is a British idiom for unintelligible talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive, deliberately ambiguous speech is called this, echoing the idiom double Dutch.

clue.text: Being snow-bound at home

parts.note: a being whose home is literally bound by snow, a dwelling built of snow blocks

explanation.surface: Someone stuck indoors by a blizzard.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional Inuit winter house, the igloo, is made of snow, so such a person lives within snow.

clue.text: Station carriage

explanation.surface: A railway terminus and a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a London terminus; a victoria is also a light four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: But he was one of Barnum's biggest attractions

definitions.text: But he was one of Barnum's biggest attractions

parts.words: But he was one of Barnum's biggest attractions
parts.note: biggest means most popular, though the performer was tiny; 'But' flags the irony

explanation.surface: A remark about a star of P. T. Barnum's circus.
explanation.definitionFit: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of Charles Stratton, a very small man who drew huge crowds for showman Barnum.

clue.text: Tibetan without money, literally

indicators.note: without tells us some letters are taken out of the word Tibetan

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A Tibetan who is penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes T, I and N (tin, money) from TIBETAN; 'literally' is a pun on 'letter', as the answer is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The second Greek alphabetic character is a letter, which 'literally' punningly suggests.

clue.text: Material for holiday wear in Norfolk?

definitions.text: Material for holiday wear in Norfolk?

parts.words: Material for holiday wear in Norfolk?
parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are a waterway holiday area, so cloth worn there might jokingly be named after them

explanation.surface: Fabric for clothes on an East Anglian break.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England popular for boating holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine woollen or cotton fabric, the name splits to suggest cloth for the Broads.

clue.text: Singer who isn't able to take a moment

parts.note: can't is the contraction of cannot, isn't able
a trice is an instant or moment

explanation.surface: A vocalist who cannot spare even a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantatrice is a borrowed word for a female professional vocalist.

clue.text: Honest, it's how the draughts man operates

definitions.text: it's how the draughts man operates

explanation.surface: Praise for the fair play of a checkers player.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; the player's hands move pieces over the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and legitimate dealing is so called; literally, a draughts player's hands work over the playing surface.

clue.text: Unhappily earls do have their trials

indicators.note: unhappily signals the letters of the following words end up badly arranged

explanation.surface: Even noblemen endure their hardships.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordeals are painful experiences that test endurance, just as trials do.

clue.text: Daring to' break off the engagement?

explanation.surface: Bravely calling off a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as de-fiancé: removing the betrothed partner. The page shows a stray apostrophe after 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is bold resistance, a daring stance; punningly, 'de-fiancé' means getting rid of one's betrothed.

clue.text: Suitable building to look round

parts.note: 'to look round' seems to mean visit, but means to appear circular in shape

explanation.surface: A building worth touring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building, often domed, so it looks round.

clue.text: Unattractive appearance of fruit on the Cape

parts.note: ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit
ness is a word for a headland or cape

explanation.surface: Fruit grown on a South African headland looks unappealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugliness is the quality of looking unpleasant, an unattractive look.

clue.text: A dance of 2 dn pace?

parts.note: the answer to 2 down means single, of which there is just one
a pace is a step

explanation.surface: A dance done at an unrivalled speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step was a ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: All the same, it's not apparent

definitions.text: All the same, it's not apparent

parts.words: All the same, it's not apparent
parts.note: if things are all the same, no distinction can be seen between them

explanation.surface: A grudging concession that nothing is visible.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinction between things is absent when they are identical, so none is seen.

clue.text: No bird in the sky for Shelley

definitions.text: No bird in the sky for Shelley

parts.words: No bird in the sky for Shelley
parts.note: Shelley's ode to a songbird of the sky says 'Bird thou never wert'

explanation.surface: A remark on the poet Shelley's view of a songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley's poem To a Skylark opens 'Hail to thee, blithe Spirit! Bird thou never wert'.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark of Shelley's poem is hailed as a spirit rather than a mere songbird.

clue.text: One concerned with the correct order of service

definitions.text: One concerned with the correct order of service

indicators.note: concerned with suggests the words that follow contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A cleric who cares about getting the liturgy right.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'cor(RECT OR)der'; the whole clue also describes a parish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest, responsible for how church services are conducted.

clue.text: Articled clerks for instance paid 100p

parts.note: 100 pence make a pound, abbreviated L
people who are paid wages are earners

explanation.surface: Trainee solicitors receive a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for a pound (Latin libra), which is 100 pence in British money; articled clerks were trainee solicitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Articled clerks are trainees, and trainees are students of their trade.

clue.text: End of scene and up she goes

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word scene
in a down entry, up reads the word and from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A stage direction: the scene closes and an actress rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's name, and any female name can stand for the pronoun.

clue.text: Essay about an undergarment? It's ridiculous!

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: to essay is to attempt, try
a vest is a British undergarment worn on the upper body

explanation.surface: Writing a composition about underwear is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A VEST inside TRY. In Britain a vest is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque parody of something, a ridiculous thing.

clue.text: Alarm causes distress in Scot

indicators.note: causes distress suggests the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A warning that upsets a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is a warning bell or signal, an alarm.

clue.text: House plant made famous in song

definitions.text: House plant made famous in song

parts.words: House plant made famous in song
parts.note: Gracie Fields sang about the biggest one in the world

explanation.surface: A potted plant celebrated in a popular tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Gracie Fields's 1938 comic song was The Biggest Aspidistra in the World.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy leafy indoor plant, much kept in Victorian parlours, became a music-hall emblem.
